title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB---.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine, one of the holdouts of the BB(6) search, halts when started on a blank tape. The halt is a Coq theorem on busycoq's definitions. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 102 (valu42, 2026-11-18) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. It reuses this repository's Coq port of DeepMind's PR 93 engine (built for 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---), started from a renamed state, and runs it to the halt. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open.

It halts, proved in Coq (theorem halt : halts tm c0 on busycoq's definitions, no axioms). With its states renamed, its table is 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0RA--- started in state D, one transition away from the table DeepMind proved halting in busycoq PR 93. DeepMind's fast engine, changed for that transition as for 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- (the same table started in B), reaches a halting configuration from state D after 688,228 engine steps, on a tape of about 26326 cells.

What it does. Before the halt the run is a cascade of halving runs: each round turns a run of n equal blocks into about n/2 blocks one level up. In the first 109 steps D read a 0 about 21,000 times, always one cell short of a halt. That description comes from simulation; the halt does not depend on it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,754 cells have been visited and 23,316 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.069). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: Moving right, A (with 1 0 behind it) and C (with 1 behind it) turn each pair 11 into 01, 6 steps a pair: a run of 2n ones becomes (01)n. Moving left, C (facing a 0) and D (facing a 1) turn each 01 back into 11, 2 steps a pair. B runs over 1s. Each holds for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: From 1 1 1 D> 0 the machine reaches F on a 1 in 3 steps and halts on the next. Conversely (by reading the table, not formalized) F is entered only from E on a 1, E only from A on a 1, and A has a 1 to its left only when it came from D on a 0, so every halt comes this way.

claims.title: Near misses: D reads a 0 next to exactly two 1s
claims.text: In the first 109 steps D reads a 0 20,887 times with 1 1 0 to its left (one 1 short of a halt) and 147 times at the blank left end; never with three 1s.

claims.title: Rounds and the halving law
claims.text: Sample the run when the head is in A at the left end of the tape (rounds; consecutive samples about 1.25 times further apart). At every sample the tape is a list of blocks 1k 00, almost all with k = 6j+1 and grouped in long runs of equal blocks, lowest level at the right. Between consecutive rounds a run of n blocks of level j becomes a run of ⌊n/2⌋−1 to ⌈n/2⌉+1 blocks of level j+1 (checked for every run of at least 10 blocks after the first 3·106 steps, to 1.7·109), and a new run of level-0 blocks 100 appears, alternately about 0.65 and 1.9 times the previous one. A few odd blocks (k = 5, 11, 17, ...) sit between the runs.

claims.title: Within a round: an expanding bouncer
claims.text: After the left-end sample the head runs right to a point well inside the tape and then zig-zags in a window whose left edge creeps left and right edge creeps right (by a few cells per bounce, using the halving and doubling rules above), until the window reaches the left end: the next sample. This is where the square-root growth on the right comes from.
claims.where: head-position trace of one round (286,681,948 to 356,669,437)

claims.title: No closed tape language from short windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with windows of K = 3, 4, 5, 6 cells finds a closed set, but every one allows a halt (72 to 145 halting abstract configurations); n-gram CPS (widths 3 to 7, with history and LRU) also fails.
claims.where: tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py; tools/c/ngramcps.c (run for the G02 group, not stored here)

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.90×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.90×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 6,642 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: The four rules where it departs from DeepMind's halting sibling
claims.text: The four changed macro rules are proved in Lean for 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---, the same table started in state C; they are statements about the table, so they hold here after the renaming of states, which is not itself checked in Lean.

claims.title: It halts: DeepMind's engine, changed for this table, proved in Coq
claims.text: The engine of busycoq PR 93, with the four rules that pass through F0 changed and every lemma built on them redone (the proof of 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---, retargeted to this table and start D), reaches a halting configuration from blank tape after 688,228 engine steps, on a tape of about 26326 cells. Coq 8.18.0 checks the run in one evaluation (about 12 hours); Print Assumptions halt: closed under the global context.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: It halts. For a long time it writes runs of equal blocks of 1s and halves them round after round, stopping one cell short of a halt thousands of times. Underneath, it is a table one transition away from a machine DeepMind proved halting, and DeepMind's engine, changed for that transition, shows in Coq that it halts.

facts.text: A Coq theorem on busycoq's definitions; the engine needs 688,228 steps, on a tape of about 2<sup>6326</sup> cells.
No halt in the C simulator; 37,754 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Each round, every run of equal blocks halves and moves up a level.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Runs of equal blocks
html: Watch the run only at the moments the head stands in state A at the left end of the tape. At every such moment the tape is a list of blocks 1k 00 (k ones, then two zeros), and almost every k has the form 6j+1: 1, 7, 13, 19, 25, ... Call j the block's level. Equal blocks come in long runs. Here is the tape at step 448,826,251, each block written as its k, x meaning repetition (so 7x570 is 570 copies of 1700):

The highest levels are on the left, the lowest on the right; the whole tape is 25,736 cells wide. The left part grows only like the logarithm of the time (a new level now and then), the right part like its square root.

sections.heading: Every run halves
html: The next sample, at step 560,017,209, reads (the leftmost few blocks left out):

Compare: the 2265 blocks of level 0 became 1133 blocks of level 1, the 570 of level 1 became 284 of level 2, 458 → 228, 113 → 56, 92 → 46, 23 → 11, 18 → 9. Every run halved and went up a level, and a fresh run of 1500 level-0 blocks appeared on the right. That is the law at every round we checked: n blocks of level j become between ⌊n/2⌋−1 and ⌈n/2⌉+1 blocks of level j+1. So a run born with n blocks survives about log2 n rounds, which is why the number of levels, and the left part of the tape, grows only logarithmically.

How the halving is done: a round is an expanding bouncer. The head runs right into the tape and then zig-zags in a window that widens on both sides a few cells per trip. Going right, it rewrites pairs of ones 11 as 01; going left it rewrites 01 back as 11 (these shift rules are proved in Lean). Doing so it eats one block of a pair and grows the other by six ones.

sections.heading: One transition away from a proved halt, and halting
html: This machine's table, with its states renamed, is 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0RA--- started in state D; 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- (state B), 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC--- (state C) are the same table started in the other two states. It differs in the single transition F0 from the table of 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---, which DeepMind proved halts (busycoq PR 93) with a fast engine: an evaluator over run-length tapes of macro words whose every step is proved sound in Coq. All of that engine's rules hold for this table except four, the ones that pass through F0. In those, where DeepMind's machine ends in the configuration <C 100, this one ends in <B 1 with 11 more on the right; on the digit words D n = 1 (11)^n 00 of the engine, this moves a carry from the digit on the left to the digit on the right.

We changed the engine at every place that uses one of the four rules (tools/coq/t4engine), extracted it from Coq to OCaml and checked it against direct simulation through 3×1010 machine steps. Run from blank tape in state D, it stops after 688,228 of its steps, on a tape of about 26326 cells, with the head in state F on a 1: a halt. The proof of the same table started in state B (holdouts/1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---/coq), which redoes DeepMind's soundness proofs for the four changed rules, needs only its table, its state map, its start and a longer final run for this machine. Coq checks the run in one evaluation, so the halt is a theorem (holdouts/1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB---/coq).

sections.heading: One cell short, until it is not
html: The machine has one halting transition (F reading a 1), and following the table backwards there is only one way into it: D reads a 0 while the three cells to its left are 1. Lean checks that 1 1 1 D> 0 halts four steps later. In the first 109 steps D read a 0 about 21,000 times, and every single time the cells to its left were 1 1 0: the block to its left had exactly two ones. So whether the machine halts is whether some round ever brings D to a 0 next to a longer run of ones, for instance through one of the odd blocks (5, 11, 17, ...) left over when a run has an odd count.

No short invariant decides it (CTL up to 6 cells, n-gram CPS up to width 7 fail), and the round map has not been worked out. The engine run above settles it without that map: much later, on a tape of about 26326 cells, D does read a 0 next to three 1s, and the machine halts after more than 101904 steps. The exact count is not computed.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.069). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,754 cells (401 left of the start, 26,856 right), with a density of 1s of 0.618.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---: rename A→C, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: Halts, proved in Coq: it is the T4 table started in D, and DeepMind's PR 93 engine changed for T4 reaches a halt after 688,228 engine steps (tape about 2^6326 cells). Before that it is a cascade of halving runs: the tape is runs of equal blocks 1^(6j+1) 00, and each round turns a run of n blocks of level j into about n/2 blocks of level j+1 (observed). Decided outside: busycoq PR 102 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here).
